title: A bounded-below torsion-cohomology object has a torsion-sheaf complex representative
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be any small site in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be its category of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Call an abelian sheaf torsion if, for every section $s\in F(U)$, there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and positive integers $n_i$ with $n_i s|_{U_i}=0$. Let $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], where $D^+$ consists of derived objects whose cohomology is zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. Suppose each $H^r(K)$ is torsion. There are an integer $a$, a cochain complex $L^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves with $L^r=0$ for $r<a$ and every $L^r$ torsion, and an isomorphism $Q(L^\bullet)\simeq K$ in $D(\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C))$, where $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. No common annihilator for the terms or for the cohomology sheaves is required.
